original_question: Can the Riemannian results that characterize when an orbit of the form gamma(t) = exp(t(a + x)) . o is a geodesic by Lie-algebraic conditions, and that characterize when a curve built from several exponential factors is geodesic, be extended from the Riemannian setting to pseudo-Riemannian homogeneous manifolds?
target_in_paper: Section 10 open problem: whether Riemannian results such as Proposition 2.2 and Proposition 9.3 can be adjusted to pseudo-Riemannian manifolds.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper's specific direction: it is not asking for a broad classification of pseudo-Riemannian g.o. spaces, but for pseudo-Riemannian analogues of two concrete Riemannian Lie-algebraic geodesic criteria. You also correctly singled out the two relevant types of curves: the one-parameter orbit gamma(t)=exp(t(a+x))·o from Proposition 2.2, and a geodesic described by a product of exponential factors from Proposition 9.3.
missing_details: The paper's exact target is the open problem in Section 10 that explicitly names Proposition 2.2 and Proposition 9.3; your draft does not identify those propositions.

To mirror those propositions, the ambient object should be a homogeneous pseudo-Riemannian space M=G/K, and in practice a reductive decomposition g=k⊕m with Ad(K)m⊂m is needed, since both propositions are formulated using the m-projection.
For the first criterion, the variables are specifically a in k and x in m, with base point o=eK.

Proposition 2.2 is more precise than 'Lie-algebraic conditions': in the Riemannian setting it gives equivalent conditions, including that gamma(t)=exp(t(a+x))·o is geodesic if and only if [a+x,Λx] lies in k, equivalently <[a+x,y]m,x>=0 for all y in m.

The operator Λ is part of the hidden setup: in Section 2 it is the metric endomorphism associated to an Ad(K)-invariant inner product on m, introduced using the negative Killing form B when G is compact semisimple.
The second cited result is not about an arbitrary number of exponential factors; Proposition 9.3 treats the specific curve gamma(t)=exp(tX)exp(tY)exp(tZ)·o with X,Y,Z in m.
Proposition 9.3 uses extra notation that your draft omits: T(t)=Ad(exp(-tZ)exp(-tY)) and the condition that GW(t) vanish identically for every W in m.

Section 8 shows that a pseudo-Riemannian analogue cannot literally copy the Riemannian statements: one must allow geodesic curves up to reparametrization, with a constant k appearing in the pseudo-Riemannian geodesic lemma, and k can be nonzero only in the null case.

Because homogeneous pseudo-Riemannian spaces need not be reductive, a faithful stand-alone question should either restrict to the reductive case or explicitly say that one seeks an analogue beyond reductive decompositions.

Your phrase 'several exponential factors' is slightly broader than the paper's actual focus; the nearest paper-faithful target is Proposition 9.3's three-factor criterion, appearing in the section on two-step homogeneous geodesics.
refined_question: For a reductive homogeneous pseudo-Riemannian space (M=G/K,g) with reductive decomposition g=k⊕m, base point o=eK, and invariant nondegenerate symmetric bilinear form on m, can one formulate and prove pseudo-Riemannian analogues of Proposition 2.2 and Proposition 9.3—compatible with the pseudo-Riemannian geodesic lemma of Section 8, so that possible reparametrization in the null case is allowed—that characterize exactly when (i) gamma(t)=exp(t(a+x))·o, with a in k and x in m, is a homogeneous geodesic, and when (ii) gamma(t)=exp(tX)exp(tY)exp(tZ)·o, with X,Y,Z in m, is a geodesic curve?
justification: The draft is aimed at the Section 10 open problem almost verbatim: the paper explicitly asks whether Riemannian results such as Proposition 2.2 and Proposition 9.3 can be adjusted to pseudo-Riemannian manifolds. Proposition 2.2 is exactly the single-exponential criterion for exp(t(a+x))·o, while Proposition 9.3 is the criterion for a product of exponential factors. Section 8 explains why any faithful pseudo-Riemannian reformulation must be modified: homogeneous geodesics are treated as geodesic curves, possibly after reparametrization, and the algebraic condition includes a constant k. I therefore sharpened your draft by making the reductive setup explicit, narrowing the multi-exponential part to the exact three-factor curve of Proposition 9.3, and incorporating the pseudo-Riemannian reparametrization issue from Lemma 8.1.

citations.label: Open problem on adjusting Propositions 2.2 and 9.3 to pseudo-Riemannian manifolds
